title: Mix the kinds of demand in a set
statement: Judge a question set as a whole: it mixes kinds of demand, such as literal, inferential and evaluative, and no one kind dominates.
example: One reading generator's set check asks for at least two of three competency areas, with none in more than 70% of the questions.
detail: A reading-question generator's quality control has a check that runs on the whole set rather than on single items: it fails a set that 'focuses too narrowly on a single competency' among literal comprehension, inferential thinking and evaluative analysis (`icloud-work/incept/incept-multilingual-generation/src/external_submodules/reading-question-qc/ck_gen - prompts.json`). A pedagogy framework in the same project asks that questions move 'from basic recall to application to reasoning' (`icloud-work/incept/incept-uae-api-website/bench.inceptapi.com/Incept Pedagogy & Learning Science Overview.md`). Both are adopted rules, with no measurement.

evidence.quote: Set should include questions from at least 2 of the 3 competency areas
No single competency should dominate (>70% of questions)
Questions move from basic recall to application to reasoning, helping students strengthen understanding step by step.
The closing must include three distinct intellectual actions.
(all seven comprehension questions literal) is by design: the 2026-09-20 ruling keeps Peter Pan reading checks literal, with inference after the you-do.
